narrative: Statutory civil remedy under PC § 290.46(j)(4)(A): actual damages or $25,000, whichever is greater, plus attorney fees, for each unlawful use of registry information. CONSERVATIVE: ~$40,000 (statutory minimum plus modest emotional distress; no wage documentation on file to support a large lost-wages claim, since Plaintiff never began working for FedEx). MODERATE: ~$95,000 (statutory penalty, ICRAA punitive damages up to $5,000 for willful noncompliance, emotional distress, and partial fee-shifting). AGGRESSIVE: ~$220,000 (treble-adjacent aggregation across all six causes of action plus Civil Code § 3294 punitive damages, if discovery yields the actual First Advantage report and confirms willful registry-based denial). Note: because Plaintiff was never hired, there are no lost W-2 wages comparable to Matter 22 — the primary economic recovery theory is the PC § 290.46(j)(4)(A) statutory penalty and lost opportunity/career-advancement damages, not back pay from an existing job.
